clue.text: Plants fruit, showing a most important craft

parts.note: flags are irises, plants of damp ground
a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: A gardener sets out plants and fruit to show off a prized handicraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests skill or handiwork, but here it means a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading vessel of a fleet, carrying the admiral's flag, is its chief ship.

clue.text: Relic of saints wrapped in thin sheet

indicators.note: the saints are enclosed by the sheet, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: foil is metal beaten into a thin sheet
S is the abbreviation for saint, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Bones of holy men are kept wrapped in foil as a church relic.
explanation.definitionFit: Remains of ancient life preserved in rock are relics of the past; also an outdated survivor.

clue.text: Get off a beam

definitions.meaning: to step down from a vehicle or horse
shining, glowing, as a face lit with joy

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for dismounting and an adjective meaning lit up or burning.

clue.text: Father accepts a time for ridicule

indicators.note: the father takes in the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A dad makes room for a moment of mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is literary mockery, using humour to ridicule folly.

clue.text: A rector in delirium is unhealthy

indicators.note: the letter A and the rector are placed inside the word for delirium

parts.note: delirium is a state of madness or insanity

explanation.surface: A clergyman raving in fever is not in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In delirium' looks like an anagram signal, but 'in' puts A R inside INSANITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Insanitary conditions are dirty ones that endanger health.

clue.text: Smirk about ship that's inferior

indicators.note: the smirk goes round the ship, so it surrounds that piece

parts.note: a leer is a sly or suggestive smirk
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a vessel that falls short of the standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesser means smaller or lower in rank, a synonym of inferior.

clue.text: Grannie's uncertain income

indicators.note: uncertain suggests the letters are unsettled and can be rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly woman is not sure how much money comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are the money one receives from work, that is, income.

clue.text: Stalker sees Bill in the rain

indicators.note: the bill is placed inside the word for the rain

parts.note: a shower is a short fall of rain
an ad, advertisement, is a bill posted up

explanation.surface: A stalker spots a man called Bill out in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is a poster, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: One who shadows another secretly follows them, as a stalker does.

clue.text: Shy soldier getting worn out

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers in crosswords
tiring means becoming weary or worn out

explanation.surface: A timid soldier is becoming exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring person is reserved and avoids company, which is to be shy.

clue.text: Medical procedure for the most destitute

definitions.meaning: a test of allergic reaction made on the skin
skint is British slang for penniless, so its superlative means poorest

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is an allergy test; read as one it is the superlative of 'skint', broke.

clue.text: Sadist conceals rare source of emotions

indicators.note: the sadist hides the other piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: a cruel person can be called a beast

explanation.surface: A cruel person hides an unusual wellspring of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: The breast is traditionally the seat of the emotions, as in 'stirred his breast'.

clue.text: Books popular present first? That's natural

indicators.note: the question asks for popular and present to come first, before the books

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
here means present, in attendance
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A question about whether well-liked current books should come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inherent is part of a thing's nature, intrinsic and natural to it.

clue.text: Tamper with setters' exactitude

parts.note: to rig is to tamper with or fix dishonestly
crossword setters speaking of themselves say 'our'

explanation.surface: Interfering with the compilers' precision.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigour is strictness and precision, a synonym of exactitude.

clue.text: Get men in to design plant

indicators.note: design here means to reshape, so these letters are rearranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Bring in workers to lay out a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignonette is a fragrant garden plant, Reseda odorata.

clue.text: Vegetable in intern's bag rotted

indicators.note: rotted implies the letters have decayed into a new order

explanation.surface: A vegetable left to go off in a trainee doctor's bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The string bean is a green bean pod eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Hamper contains flimsy dress

indicators.note: the hamper holds the other piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: to clog is to hamper or obstruct
thin means flimsy, lacking substance

explanation.surface: A laundry basket holds a skimpy frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a basket, which suits the dress inside; it is the verb, to clog.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress as a mass noun means garments in general, that is, clothing.

clue.text: Mockery is undesirable in advancing years

parts.note: bad means undesirable or unwelcome
age means old age, advancing years

explanation.surface: Teasing is unwelcome as one gets older.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful banter and teasing, a light form of mockery.

clue.text: Yokel holds hearts in game

indicators.note: the yokel contains the other piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: a peasant is a country bumpkin, a yokel
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A country fellow holds the heart suit during a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearts in game' suggests cards; game here means shot birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Game is wild birds or animals hunted for sport, and the pheasant is a classic example.

clue.text: Punishment for having mead before opera cycle

indicators.note: before places the meadow ahead of the opera cycle in the answer

parts.note: mead is an old word for meadow, as is lea
The Ring is Wagner's cycle of four operas

explanation.surface: A punishment for drinking honey wine ahead of a Wagner marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mead' looks like the honey drink; it is the poetic word for meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A leathering is a thrashing, a beating given as punishment, originally with a strap.

clue.text: Prominence of Hungary's rowing team

parts.note: H is the international vehicle code for Hungary
an eight is a racing boat crewed by eight rowers

explanation.surface: Hungary's crew has risen to fame on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A height is a raised place, a prominence in the landscape.

clue.text: Consequence of queen tucking into cooked eels

indicators.note: the queen goes inside, as food is tucked into
cooked suggests the eels are prepared and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: The monarch eats a dish of eels, with consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' is here the two-letter abbreviation rather than the usual single letter; 'cooked' and 'tucking into' are the two indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequel is what follows from something, its result or consequence.

clue.text: Lack of interest in a youth leader crossing road

indicators.note: A and the youth's first letter span the road, one on each side
leader means the first letter of youth

parts.note: a path is a way or road

explanation.surface: A bored teenager who heads the group crosses the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is indifference, a lack of interest or concern.

clue.text: Paint a curious snake

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: Paint an odd-looking serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: The taipan is a highly venomous Australian snake.

clue.text: Want to be in castle and heavily involved

indicators.note: the want goes inside the castle

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
to need is to want or lack

explanation.surface: Someone longs to be in the castle and gets thoroughly embroiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Knee-deep in something means deeply immersed or involved in it.

clue.text: Fleming toured corrupt African city

indicators.note: Fleming goes round the corrupt piece, so it sits inside

parts.note: Ian Fleming was the author of the James Bond novels
bad means corrupt or rotten

explanation.surface: The Bond author travelled round a crooked city in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibadan is a large city in south-western Nigeria.

clue.text: Accident claims Mark in chase

indicators.note: the accident takes the mark inside itself

parts.note: a shunt is British slang for a minor car crash
a tag is a label or mark

explanation.surface: A crash takes Mark's life during a pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: SHUNT is British slang for a minor road collision.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag hunt is the chasing of deer on horseback with hounds, a chase.

clue.text: Greek devours the classics

parts.note: eats means devours

explanation.surface: A Greek gobbles up the old literature.
explanation.walkthrough: Greats is the Oxford name for the Classics degree course.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford, Greats is the course of study in Classics, Latin and Greek literature and philosophy.

clue.text: People count in their heads

parts.note: men means people, persons
a tally is a count or reckoning

explanation.surface: Folk do arithmetic without pen and paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something mentally means doing it in the mind, in one's head.
